editedExercise.name: Bodyweight Squat

instructions.description: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart or slightly wider, with your toes pointing slightly outward. Keep your chest upright, engage your core, and extend your arms forward for balance.
Bend your knees and push your hips back as if you were sitting into a chair. Keep your entire foot firmly planted on the floor and allow your knees to track in line with your toes.
Lower yourself as far as you can comfortably go while maintaining good control and a neutral spine. Keep your chest lifted and avoid letting your heels rise or your knees collapse inward.
Press evenly through your feet and drive your hips forward to return to a standing position. Keep your core engaged and exhale as you stand.

variations.variationDescription: Goblet Squat meaningfully changes the difficulty, loading, support, or movement demands compared with Bodyweight Squat.

variationSuggestions.variationDescription: Bodyweight Squat — Tempo-Controlled Version: Use a deliberately slower lowering phase without creating a separate database record.
Bodyweight Squat — Reduced-Range Version: Use a smaller comfortable range while preserving the same movement pattern.

commentsNotes: Use a chair behind you as an optional depth guide.
Your arms can move forward naturally as you descend to help with balance and stability.
Keep your knees tracking in the same direction as your toes rather than letting them collapse inward.
